Digimon World -next 0rder- (Vita)
English Patch v

Introduction

The definitive way to play on PlayStation Vita!

This patch brings the full English translation to the Japanese and Chinese versions of Digimon World -next 0rder- for PlayStation Vita. It's based on the unused partial English translation found in the game's files, with missing parts of text backported from the International Edition. Thousands of tweaks, edits, and full-fledged retranslations were made to improve the quality of the text and fix UI flaws and other cosmetic issues where possible.

Download Patch v from Google Drive Join the Discord Server

Patch variants

This English translation patch comes in two variants:

  • For the Japanese PS Vita release of the game (PCSG00792)
  • For the Chinese PS Vita release of the game (PCSH00261)

In the Japanese version, you can NOT use Latin characters in the player name and Digimon nicknames. You'll be forced to either leave the pre-filled default Japanese names for everything, or enter your own names in full-width katakana. The game's LiveArea assets, its bubble name on your PS Vita home screen, and all the trophies will be in Japanese.

In the Chinese version, you CAN use Latin characters for names. But the game's LiveArea assets, its bubble name on your PS Vita home screen, and all the trophies will be in Chinese.

Other than these nuances, the game is 100% in English in both variants of the patch, so choose the one that sounds more appealing to you. For example, I (the author of the patch) prefer having LiveArea assets and trophies in Japanese instead of Chinese, which even outweighs the ability to have an English in-game name for me. But I can't imagine this being the case for the majority of players, so I expect the Chinese variant to be the one most commonly used.

Requirements

Your PlayStation Vita console needs to be modded with CFW.
You also need NoNpDrm, rePatch, and possibly 0syscall6.

Alternatively, you can try emulating the game using Vita3K emulator.
In this case, a good experience is not guaranteed.

Installing the Japanese version

(You can only enter katakana for names in this version.)

On a Sony PlayStation Vita console:

  • Install the Japanese version of the game (title ID: PCSG00792), along with its latest update v1.05 and all available DLC.
  • Transfer the repatch/PCSG00792 folder from the extracted patch archive to ux0:repatch on your console (create that folder if needed).

On Vita3K emulator:

  • Install the Japanese version of the game (title ID: PCSG00792), along with its latest update v1.05 and all available DLC.
  • In Vita3K, go to File → Install Archive → Select a file, then select the archive with the patch. The archive contains variations for both versions of the game (Japanese and Chinese). The emulator will report that installing the patch for the version you don't have installed has "Failed." This is normal. The one for the version you have should say "Installed."
Installing the Chinese version

(You can enter English letters for names in this version.)

On a Sony PlayStation Vita console:

  • Install the Chinese version of the game (title ID: PCSH00261), along with its latest update v1.03 and all available DLC.
  • Transfer the repatch/PCSH00261 folder from the extracted patch archive to ux0:repatch on your console (create that folder if needed).

On Vita3K emulator:

  • Install the Chinese version of the game (title ID: PCSH00261), along with its latest update v1.03 and all available DLC.
  • In Vita3K, go to File → Install Archive → Select a file, then select the archive with the patch. The archive contains variations for both versions of the game (Japanese and Chinese). The emulator will report that installing the patch for the version you don't have installed has "Failed." This is normal. The one for the version you have should say "Installed."
Wasn't there already an English patch?

An old incomplete patch for the Chinese version of the game has been floating around on the internet for years. It was playable, but had too many flaws, because it was made by simply swapping the language files with the unused English ones found in the game's resource archive, and nothing more. Those files are incomplete, and a lot of text is missing from them altogether, resulting in some parts of the game being unplayable and some options inaccessible due to their text strings being omitted (which leads to some text boxes and menu items being empty). There's also the cosmetic aspect: the unused English translation was seemingly not intended for Vita (it was probably only included in its files for testing purposes in preparation for the International Edition), so the text often doesn't fit the UI and overflows. Also, the font used for English text didn't look good at all.

What makes the new English patch better?

Compared to the old patch, this one has everything translated, with no omitted text. A lot of effort was put into altering the text to make it fit the UI as nicely as possible without actually hacking the game's code. The text was also heavily edited to improve its overall quality significantly. The translation included in the Vita version's files seems like a pre-pre-alpha product, with the English text often not making any sense. Its tutorials constantly lie to the player and explain gameplay mechanics incorrectly, characters spout nonsense on a regular basis, terminology is inconsistent, often wrong, and changes back and forth. At least 50% of the text (maybe more) was likely machine-translated.

I made it my mission to improve the sorry state of it all. This took a lot of time and effort, but there should be much less nonsense in the game's text as a result. Also, work has been done to restore all the dub names and terminology to the original (Japanese) ones.

I've decided to call the new patch "v2" to help distinguish it from the old one.

Funnily enough, with all this you're actually getting a far better localization compared to the modern official English release (the International Edition), which actually contains Vita version's unused pre-alpha nonsensical text amost as is, additionally dubbed by human actors.
